components.css: .ds-arrow-link { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.35rem; font: 600 1rem/1.65 var(--font, 'Hanken Grotesk', sans-serif); color: var(--ink, #e2e8f0); text-decoration: none; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule, #1f2a3d); transition: border-color 0.2s, color 0.2s; } .ds-arrow-link svg { transition: transform 0.25s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-arrow-link:hover { color: var(--accent, #5eead4); border-color: var(--accent, #5eead4); } .ds-arrow-link:hover svg { transform: translate(2px, -2px); } .ds-arrow-link:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #5eead4); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.css: .ds-nav { display: flex; flex-direction: column; } .ds-nav a { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 1rem; padding: 0.6rem 0; text-decoration: none; font: 600 0.75rem/1.65 var(--font, 'Hanken Grotesk', sans-serif); letter-spacing: 0.12em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--faint, #7d8ba1); transition: color 0.2s; } .ds-nav a::before { content: ''; height: 1px; width: 2rem; background: currentColor; transition: width 0.35s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-nav a:hover, .ds-nav a.active { color: var(--ink, #e2e8f0); } .ds-nav a:hover::before, .ds-nav a.active::before { width: 4rem; } .ds-nav a.active::before { background: var(--accent, #5eead4); } .ds-nav a:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #5eead4); outline-offset: 3px; }

narrative.overview:
The page is a resume given room to breathe: a deep navy sheet, one pale ink, one teal, and hairlines where a printed CV would have rules. It takes the category-standard engineer-portfolio layout (sticky identity column on the left, scrolling evidence on the right) and refuses to decorate it. Every visual decision exists to move a recruiter's eye from name to measured result in under a minute.

Density is moderate and list-like. Content sits in rows separated by 1px hairlines, never in cards. The only color that is not a navy or slate is the teal accent, and it appears on interaction (links, hover, the active nav line) and on the technology pills. Numbers are the loudest thing in the body copy: tabular numerals everywhere, and measured results set in ink at weight 600 against slate prose.

Motion is small and functional: the nav line extends, an arrow nudges up-right, sibling rows dim. Nothing animates on load.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-only navy ground, single pale ink, single teal accent.
Two columns on desktop (5fr / 7fr), left column sticky at full viewport height.
Hairline-separated rows; no cards, no shadows.
Tabular numerals globally; metrics bolded in ink inside slate prose.
One typeface (Hanken Grotesk) across every role.

rules.name: The One Teal Rule
rules.body: Signal Teal is the only hue. It marks interaction, the resume outline, and technology tags; it never fills a section, a background band, or a heading.

rules.name: The Ink-for-Proof Rule
rules.body: In running prose, ink is reserved for measured results (percentages, multipliers, throughput, money, counts). Prose stays slate so the numbers surface on a skim.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums is set on body and inherited everywhere; dates and metrics must align and never jitter.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Every role uses Hanken Grotesk. Do not introduce a second display or mono face.

rules.name: The Rail Rule
rules.body: Metadata (dates, thumbnails) lives in a fixed-width left rail of each row; titles and prose always start on the same vertical line.

rules.name: The Flat Sheet Rule
rules.body: Nothing lifts off the page. Separation is a 1px hairline or whitespace, never a shadow or a filled card.

dos: Do keep Signal Teal to interaction states, focus, selection, the resume outline, and tags.
Do separate list items with a 1px hairline and 1.5rem padding, first row unruled.
Do bold measured results in ink inside slate prose.
Do use tabular numerals for any date or metric.
Do keep motion to color shifts, line extension, 2px arrow nudges, and sibling dimming; respect reduced motion.
donts: Don't put content in cards or add box-shadows.
Don't introduce a second accent hue or a second typeface.
Don't set a tracked uppercase label above a heading as a kicker; uppercase labels are for the nav and the mobile section bars only.
Don't animate content in on load or on scroll.
